verdict: Of the 29 distinct critical-or-major audit findings (after de-duplicating items raised by several auditors), I accept 28 and reject 1. Accepted and independently confirmed by me: the CASCADE_PINS abort (autodock_exhaustiveness_returns.py:214-217, :1375 — the only critical, and it also strands plan step 2.4); the PandaMap crystal-reference gate that keeps single-instance natives unless the two crystal CSVs are removed (run_pandamap.py:1174-1176, 07_benchmark_pandamap.yaml:67, files dated 2026-08-14); the five crystal.groupby unions in pandamap_interaction_report.py:1185/:1484/:1729/:2435 and interaction_pose_basis_audit.py:227/:406; the omitted bench_ligand/receptor_difficulty stages (_build_reproduction_notebook.py:623-638) so the 3.2 count is 15 named of 19 (16 counting bench_pose_comparison itself — the two auditors' 15-vs-16 is a counting basis, not a conflict); the undecided benchmark_full_protein_vina_scoring tree (defaults at thesis_endpoint_diagnostics.py:40, optimization_benefit_stats.py:348, autodock_exhaustiveness_returns.py:221, rebust_hydrogen_normalised.py:65-67); D9's single-copy row being RMSD-only (my recompute 90/84/54 of 165 vs 88/80/53 with the validity gate); Section 7's "Sections 4.2 and 5.2" (Thesis_short.toc:43 makes 5.2 the validity/optimisation section holding the :777 "at most four" sentence; Orai1 is 5.5 at toc:46); the plan's table numbering (Thesis_short.lot: 2 = depth recovery, 3 = cluster reach, 4 = interaction, 6 = cost, 8 = ladder; the plan's "Table 5/6/7/8" and "Tables 2-3 dataset" are wrong and 7.1 contradicts Section 7); Section 1.5's mixed bases (body_appendix_short.tex:949 prints 21/39, p 0.0273, not 0.040; 39/20 belongs to the validity-gated :843 sentence); the +2 appendix line shift (git hunk @@ -463,7 +463,9 @@; ITT now :1074, convention :666) — correct in substance though mechanical; the 7Z1Q_NIO refutation of the :664 draft (three PB-valid ladder poses at 1.70-1.75 Å from the alternate); the 25 Å cube overstatement (8 of 211 alternate centroids inside the half-edge); the 99.7 vs 99.3 % reach inconsistency between D2 and D5 (297/301/302 of 303 under centroid_dist/cd_nearest/cd_min_all); the 7JHQ_VAJ metal-stratum disagreement (copy 0 at 2.42 Å from Na, copies 1-3 at 21.8-39.5 Å); 47 not 26 Kabsch cells; the top-15 form tie moving to p_holm 0.899 (30/32 is the largest p in its three-pair family) while :396 prints 1.000; Risk 2's "three arms" being five printed Table 1 rows (the plan's own 1.3 table shows fpocket 180→179 and P2Rank 181→180) with no disclosure anywhere in Phase 5 or the D9 table; the Table 19 star flips (5/17 → p 0.0169 × Holm multiplier 4 = 0.0676) and the D14 Holm-family decision; the 8.2→11.7 mis-mapping in row 1256-1258 (MDD at n = 428 is 8.8); the :246 plateau argument collapsing rather than renumbering; D10's unstated scope at :230; the missing inspection of the eight flips in (1.5, 2.0] Å; the incomplete 1.11 regression (four columns asserted while contact/PLIF/torsion/pb_rmsd_within_2A also move; 241,913 rows; oracle_summary gains no columns); meta.reference_convention being read by nothing; Phase 6's md5 hand-check and validate_regeneration gates being blind to the convention and to a stale cluster cache (_CACHE_SCHEMA = 5 at pose_cluster_crystal_pocket_report.py:3927, path-keyed crystal dirs at :3947-3949). Rejected as a major: the numbers-selection completeness claim that a Phase 0 probe of equibind_fpocket_gnina/equibind_p2rank_gnina is required before Phase 5 — per_pose_metrics.csv already carries both keys and the Phase 3.1 hub rebuild scores all 27 method keys before any Phase 5 wording is written, so the residue is the appendix-evidence minor that Section 1.3's "179-199" range rests on five of nine EquiBind configurations and must be labelled recompute. Everything in the plan's Section 1.1, 1.2 and D12 headline tables survived every auditor's recomputation; the plan's failures are sequencing (pins, PandaMap gate, cache schemas), undecided or self-contradicting decisions (D2 vs D5 reach, D4 membership, D9 basis, D10 scope, Holm family), and stale anchors, not the endpoint numbers themselves.

gaps.what: D8 sequencing is internally inconsistent: D8 (plan line 36) says the default flips to `nearest` 'in the same commit that edits the stage command', but step 1.12 (line 259) flips the default in Phase 1 while the stage-command edit is step 7.3 (line 331), five phases later; Phase 3.1 (line 273) passes the flag explicitly, so the harness stage is fine, but between 1.12 and 7.3 any bare `posebusters_pose_comparison.py` call or Master_Docking_AD_Full_Protein.ipynb cell[33] rebuilds under `nearest` with no flag and, because the convention enters `_per_pose_signature` (1.9), the manifest mismatch triggers an unrequested full recompute rather than a refusal.
gaps.why_it_matters: It is exactly the silent-convention-switch risk D8 exists to prevent, and the plan's own Risk 5 (line 508) describes it for the reuse-cache path only.
gaps.how_to_fill: Move the stage-command edit (builder :386-400) and the notebook cell[33] flag into step 1.12, or keep the default at `instance` until Phase 7 and pass `--reference-convention nearest` explicitly everywhere in Phases 3-6; add a check that `git grep -n 'posebusters_pose_comparison.py' -- '*.ipynb' '*.py' '*.md'` shows the flag on every invocation.

gaps.what: Step 2.4 (line 266) has no valid slot in the order: it asks to run `autodock_exhaustiveness_returns.py` 'as the first consumer to prove the coupling holds' inside Phase 2, i.e. before the Phase 3 rebuild exists, where it can only re-read the single-instance table and proves nothing about D2; after the rebuild it aborts before reaching the :570 coupling assert because CASCADE_PINS (autodock_exhaustiveness_returns.py:214-217) pins exh18 to 126/160/1.8 and exh92 to 194/290/3.2 and main() raises SystemExit at :1375.
gaps.why_it_matters: The plan's only executable proof that `bestfit_rmsd == pb_kabsch_rmsd` survives D2 never runs, and the first bench_exhaustiveness_returns stage of Phase 3.2 fails with a regression message that reads like a bug in the switch.
gaps.how_to_fill: Move 2.4 to immediately after 3.1; precede it with a re-pin step that recomputes CASCADE_PINS from the rebuilt ladder (or makes the pins convention-keyed via the manifest); record the expected new pins (exh18 144/219/2.4, exh92 209/407/4.5 from nearest_copy_ladder_arms.csv) as the check, not the old ones.

gaps.what: Phase 0.4 (line 244) and Risk 11 (line 518) trace only two pre-existing drifts (:476 reach, :408 clip count). At least five more printed values already disagree with their generators or with each other under the CURRENT convention and would be overwritten with the offset carried forward: body_main_short.tex:113 'adds three recovered complexes' (my recompute from per_pose_two_conventions.csv on rank-1 PB-valid rows gives fully-symmetrised-gate additions of 1/0/1 = two under both conventions); :396 'p_holm <= 4e-10' vs the companion report's 8.997e-09; :414 '2.9 Å' vs Table 27's 2.977 (rounds to 3.0); :474 '55.4 %' vs the sidecar's 55.5 %; :781 'gnina is level or ahead on every component' vs :199's form 237 vs 235 (smina ahead).
gaps.why_it_matters: The plan's Risk 11 rationale ('or the new numbers inherit an unexplained offset') applies to all seven, and an examiner comparing regenerated sidecars with the prose will find the same class of drift the switch was meant to clean up.
gaps.how_to_fill: Extend 0.4 to a table of every printed value whose generator disagrees today (:113, :396, :408, :414, :474, :476, :781), name the generator and basis for each, and decide per line whether the printed value or the generator is corrected before Phase 5 writes new numbers on top.

gaps.what: D4 (line 33) and step 2.6 (line 269) assume a registrable generator for the 78-complex metal-adjacent stratum, but no rule under Scripts/ reproduces 78 (an element-based 5 Å rule on the reference instance gives 77 of 303 per the methodology audit), and membership is copy-dependent: for 7JHQ_VAJ the reference copy lies 2.42 Å from a Na ion while copies 1-3 are 21.8/22.5/39.5 Å away (my recompute from Data/PoseBuster Benchmark Set/7JHQ_VAJ/7JHQ_VAJ_protein.pdb and _ligands.sdf), and its AutoDock* rank-1 pose flips to near-native on copy 3. The plan has no fallback if 78 cannot be regenerated and no rule for a pose scored on a copy in the other stratum.
gaps.why_it_matters: Section 7 lists 'Metal-adjacent stratum size 78' as unchanged and :868/App. C :165 print stratum contrasts (+6.7 / +20.5 pp) that the plan marks recompute; without a reproducible rule the recompute has no executor and the 78 cannot be asserted by the harness.
gaps.how_to_fill: Add a Phase 0 decision: try the candidate rules (element set, 4/5/6 Å, HETATM-only vs any metal) against the reference instance and record which reproduces 78; if none does, define the stratum from the registered rule and accept the count change in :88/:868/:165; state explicitly that stratum membership stays a reference-instance property and that a pose recovered on a metal-free copy is still counted in its complex's stratum, with the number of such complexes disclosed.

gaps.what: The preamble to Section 2 (line 243) promises 'Every step names its verification check', but Phase 5 (steps 5.1-5.6, lines 280-292) names none, and the Phase 8.2 registry sweep (line 345) lists old values from Sections 1 and 3.2 only; it omits the appendix descriptive values that the audits show also move (98/128/149/159/164 at :230, 93/183 and 94/185 at :184, 'only two of the seven' at :182, 8.2 and 4,200 at :1260, 31.4/37.3 and 21/39 at :949, 30 against 31 at :396, 'exactly 113' at :246, 1.490/1.543 and 1.467/1.566 at :1387).
gaps.why_it_matters: Phase 5 is the largest phase (2-3 days) and the one where the appendix +2 line shift already shows how anchors go stale; without a mechanical check, a missed sentence survives to the examiner exactly as the current stale Orai1 paragraphs did.
gaps.how_to_fill: Generate the 8.2 sweep list programmatically from the 'Current' column of the Section 3.1-3.3 tables plus every number in the audits' 'missing' items, anchor Phase 5 edits by quoted text rather than line number, and make the per-step check 'grep of the short build for the old literal returns only the legitimately retained hits recorded in a table'.

gaps.what: Risk 15 (line 525) states the yaml transcription direction but no step operationalises it: there is no negative-control run of `thesis_assertions.py` against the rebuilt outputs with the OLD yaml before 7.1 re-transcribes ~850 rows, so a re-transcription that accidentally copies outputs into the yaml (the Table 21 drift the risk cites) is indistinguishable from a genuine pass at 8.3.
gaps.why_it_matters: The harness currently prints 1364/1364; after 7.1 it will print a new all-pass total whether or not the values came from the printed thesis, and the plan offers no artefact that proves which rows changed and by how much.
gaps.how_to_fill: Insert between 3.2 and 7.1: run `thesis_assertions.py` unchanged against the rebuilt tree, save the mismatch report as the change signature (expected roughly 850 mismatching rows, every one in a block Section 4 lists as changing, none in cohort/determinism/Orai blocks), and require 7.1's re-transcribed yaml to fail against the FROZEN backup tree (0.3) with the same signature.

gaps.what: Section 3.3 rows carry no gate-basis column, and the appendix itself is inconsistent about it: body_appendix_short.tex:871 introduces the top-k tables as 'rank-1 validity-aware recovery (34.0 % and 34.3 %)' while the Table 19 rows at :949-956 are near-native WITHOUT the validity gate (33.7 → 35.3 for DiffDock + smina is 102/303 → 107/303). This ambiguity is what produced the Section 1.5 mix-up (39/20 gated values attached to the 43.2 → 49.8 ungated percentages), the Table 19 star losses at k = 5 (5/17, p 0.0169, Holm × 4 = 0.0676) and the two conflicting Holm families for the AutoDock raw→gnina step (:182 seven-contrast family survives, Table 19 sixteen-test family does not).
gaps.why_it_matters: Every appendix table in Section 3.3 and the corresponding yaml blocks (table_18/19/20/21/22) can be transcribed on the wrong gate without any check catching it, and the body's :843 'does not clear Holm' sentence will contradict App. C :182 unless the family is named.
gaps.how_to_fill: Add a 'gate' column (near-native only / PB-valid ∧ ≤ 2 Å / triple) to every Section 3.2 and 3.3 row and to the yaml block comments, fix the :871 lead-in to the basis the tables use, and record a D14 naming the Holm family the body quotes for the raw→gnina step.

gaps.what: The plan's derived-versus-recompute bookkeeping is inconsistent with its own Phase 3: step 5.4 says :77 'needs probe run on the vinardo arms' and Section 3.3 row 267-269 prints a '179-199' Form range for all nine EquiBind configurations although the probe covers five (per_pose_metrics.csv carries equibind_fpocket_gnina and equibind_p2rank_gnina, absent from scratchpad/wf/nearest_copy_guided_equibind_arms.csv), while other values marked 'recompute' are derivable now (Table 8 rungs, Table 26 Kabsch half, Table 21 Holm). Meanwhile the five wf_plan helper scripts (kabsch_nearest*.py, itt_dropped_ids.py, pb_loadall_replicate.py) that produced the two-convention CSVs import hub functions and are neither registered nor archived (2.7 mentions only nearest_copy_rescoring.py), and the probe README's sensitivity framing inverts after the switch.
gaps.why_it_matters: Two parallel sources of truth (probe CSVs and the rebuilt hub table) with no rule for which wins invites transcribing a probe preview into the thesis where the hub value differs (the EquiBind-raw ordering already does not reproduce from the probe: 3.3/5.3 vs printed 3.0/4.0 at k = 5/10).
gaps.how_to_fill: State one rule in Section 1: probe values are previews used only to write expectations in advance; every printed number comes from the Phase 3 rebuild; the Vinardo and guided-gnina arms need no probe because 3.1 scores all 27 method keys. Archive the five helper scripts and the probe CSVs read-only under the new bench_reference_convention stage directory and rewrite nearest_copy_probe/README.md:5 so rmsd_ref_re is checked against rmsd_ref_instance.
